node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinate axes
node.description: Identify and use horizontal and vertical axes in the Cartesian coordinate plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ordered pairs
node.description: Interpret ordered pairs as coordinates giving horizontal and vertical positions.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Plot points in first quadrant
node.description: Plot and read points in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Four quadrants
node.description: Locate and plot points across all four quadrants using positive and negative coordinates.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Horizontal and vertical distance
node.description: Find horizontal and vertical distances between points on a coordinate plane.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Context points on graphs
node.description: Interpret coordinate points as paired quantities in a context.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Input output tables
node.description: Represent relationships between two variables using tables of input and output values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Linear rules from tables
node.description: Identify and write linear rules from patterns in tables of values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Graph linear rules
node.description: Graph linear relationships from tables, rules or equations.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportional linear relationships
node.description: Recognise proportional relationships as linear relationships passing through the origin.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nonproportional linear relationships
node.description: Recognise linear relationships with a nonzero starting value or intercept.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Rate of change in tables
node.description: Use tables to identify constant additive change and constant rate of change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Linear equations from contexts
node.description: Write linear equations to model contextual relationships between two quantities.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gradient as rate of change
node.description: Interpret gradient as the rate at which one variable changes relative to another.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gradient from two points
node.description: Calculate gradient using the change in vertical values divided by the change in horizontal values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Y intercept meaning
node.description: Interpret the y-intercept as the output value when the input is zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Slope intercept form
node.description: Represent linear relationships using slope-intercept form and interpret its parameters.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: X intercept meaning
node.description: Interpret the x-intercept as the input value that makes the output zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Recognise nonlinear graphs
node.description: Recognise graphs that do not have a constant rate of change or straight-line form.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare linear and nonlinear rate
node.description: Compare constant rate of change in linear graphs with changing rates in nonlinear graphs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Quadratic graph shape
node.description: Recognise quadratic graphs by their parabolic shape and changing rate of change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ordered pair order matters
node.description: In an ordered pair, the first coordinate and second coordinate describe different axes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Coordinates can be negative
node.description: Coordinate values can be positive, zero or negative depending on location relative to the axes.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Tables graphs and equations connect
node.description: Tables, graphs and equations can represent the same relationship between variables.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Linear relationship has constant rate
node.description: A linear relationship changes by a constant amount for equal changes in input.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Proportional graph passes through origin
node.description: A proportional linear relationship has a graph that passes through the origin.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gradient is rise over run
node.description: Gradient compares vertical change to horizontal change between points on a line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Y intercept is starting value
node.description: In many contexts, the y-intercept represents the starting value when input is zero.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Slope intercept parameters have meaning
node.description: In slope-intercept form, the gradient and intercept describe different features of the line.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Nonlinear rate changes
node.description: A nonlinear relationship does not have the same rate of change over every equal input interval.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Intercepts are axis crossings
node.description: Intercepts are points where a graph crosses an axis.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Reverse ordered pair
node.description: Learner plots or reads coordinates by reversing the x and y values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Axes are interchangeable
node.description: Learner treats the horizontal and vertical axes as interchangeable without regard to variable meaning.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Every line is proportional
node.description: Learner assumes every straight-line graph represents a proportional relationship.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Gradient is height
node.description: Learner identifies gradient using only vertical height rather than comparing vertical and horizontal change.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Curved graphs are not functions
node.description: Learner assumes nonlinear or curved graphs cannot represent functions or relationships.

edge.rationale: Axes are foundational parts of coordinate plane work.
Ordered pairs are central to locating points in a coordinate plane.
First-quadrant plotting is early coordinate-plane practice.
Four-quadrant plotting extends coordinate plane work to signed coordinates.
Horizontal and vertical distances are coordinate-plane applications.
Context points apply coordinates to paired quantities.
Input-output tables are a core representation of relationships.
Finding rules from tables links tabular and symbolic representations.
Graphing linear rules is a central linear-functions skill.
Proportional relationships are an important linear case.
Nonproportional linear relationships contrast constant rate with nonzero initial value.
Constant rate of change is central to linear relationships.
Context equations apply linear relationships symbolically.
Gradient is the rate-of-change feature of a linear graph.
Calculating gradient from two points is a core gradient skill.
Y-intercept interpretation is central to linear graph structure.
Slope-intercept form combines gradient and y-intercept in an equation.
X-intercepts extend intercept reasoning to the horizontal axis.
Recognising nonlinear graphs is foundational for this broad topic.
Contrasting rates of change separates linear from nonlinear relationships.
Quadratic graphs are common early nonlinear graphs.
Coordinate axes extend grid and map-location reasoning into algebraic coordinates.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot orient horizontal and vertical reference lines on a grid.

edge.rationale: Ordered pairs refer to positions along coordinate axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect first and second coordinates to axes.

edge.rationale: Plotting points requires interpreting ordered pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reverses or misreads coordinates when plotting.

edge.rationale: Four-quadrant coordinates require positive and negative numbers on both axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot place points with negative coordinates in the correct quadrant.

edge.rationale: Coordinate distances require reading positions and differences along axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts diagonal movement or subtracts coordinates without considering direction and axis.

edge.rationale: Contextual graph points require interpreting coordinates as paired quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner plots the point but cannot explain what each coordinate means.

edge.rationale: Input-output tables use variables to represent related quantities.
edge.failure_signal: Learner lists values but cannot identify input and output variables.

edge.rationale: Writing rules from tables requires reading input-output pairs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes a table recursively but cannot express the relationship as a rule.

edge.rationale: Graphing linear rules requires plotting points from a table or equation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner creates values but cannot plot them accurately as points.

edge.rationale: Proportional linear relationships build directly from proportional reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats any increasing straight line as proportional even without passing through the origin.

edge.rationale: Nonproportional linear relationships require recognising a constant rate plus starting value.
edge.failure_signal: Learner expects all linear relationships to be proportional.

edge.rationale: Rate of change in tables builds from unit-rate reasoning.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares output differences without relating them to input changes.

edge.rationale: Writing equations from contexts requires identifying a relationship rule between variables.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes an expression that does not model the context's relationship.

edge.rationale: Gradient formalises constant rate of change represented in tables and graphs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads steepness visually but cannot connect it to rate of change.

edge.rationale: Calculating gradient from two points depends on interpreting gradient as rate of change.
edge.failure_signal: Learner subtracts coordinates without forming vertical change over horizontal change.

edge.rationale: Y-intercept interpretation requires reading a linear graph and its axes.
edge.failure_signal: Learner identifies the intercept visually but cannot connect it to input zero.

edge.rationale: Slope-intercept form requires interpreting the gradient parameter of a line.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes y = mx + b but cannot interpret m or b.

edge.rationale: X-intercepts extend intercept reasoning to the horizontal axis, though the dependency is representational rather than procedural.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses which coordinate is zero at an axis crossing.

edge.rationale: Recognising nonlinear graphs depends on contrasting them with linear graphs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner calls any graph with plotted points linear or treats all relationships as straight lines.

edge.rationale: Comparing rates requires first recognising linear and nonlinear graph forms.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot explain why a curve's rate changes.

edge.rationale: Quadratic graphs are a common nonlinear graph family introduced after recognising nonlinear shape.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a parabola as a bent line without recognising its changing rate.
